corrected: §10.5 gets the sources wrong. SLOW, WOUND and CRIT_DOWN come from the `slow`/`wound`/`critDown` fields of a DoT DAMAGE spell at cast (L1092079-1092190). DEBUFF spells apply only their own `debuffType`, with `spell.debuff` as config (L1091685-1091700); that type can be WOUND (one catalogue DEBUFF spell), BLEED or POISON, so the bleed/poison `damagePerTickPercent` debuff also belongs to DEBUFF spells. Blind is `blindOnTick` on each DoT tick (L1091236); there is no `blinds` field. The engine already does all of this correctly; only the doc needs fixing. | The finding is right, with two adjustments. - Blind is `blindOnTick`, checked on each DoT tick (L1091236).

corrected: Sigil activation conditions are character-wide in the game (one per owned sigil species). The app models and optimises them per preset, so it can hold or suggest conflicting per-preset conditions for a shared sigil and mis-score the other presets that equip it. The practical effect is limited to buff/heal conditions in PvE, plus PvP for all spell types. data-model.md line 115 contradicts sigils.md §7.
fixNotes: Preferred fix: move the condition to sigils.owned[sp].condition and update data-model.md. Cheaper alternative: when applying or scoring a condition change, propagate it to all presets that equip that species, or warn about the others.

title: Ancient sigil can be paired with a transcendence preset that does not allocate its sigil node; the game grants
failureScenario: The fixture's 'alt' transcendence preset has no sig_13,-25 node, but the candidate {transcendencePresetId: 'alt', ancientSigilSpecies: 'FLAMEBORN'} is offered and scored with Flameborn's +6000*tier Attack / +40000*tier HP and transform. If the server revokes the Ancient when a board without its node becomes active (the client plumbing exists, but the rule itself is [SERVER]), the suggestion is unrealisable. Unconfirmed: the server rule is unknown.
proposedFix: At minimum, document the open question in transcendence.md/sigils.md. If it is confirmed, tie ancient availability to the candidate's transcendence preset (allocatedNodeIds includes the node from ANCIENT_SIGIL_BY_TRANSCENDENCE_NODE) and filter the ancient pool per candidate.

title: Transcendence move offers 'default' when the preset's link is null: an inert change (same board)
failureScenario: For a new preset (transcendencePresetId null, data-model default) one evaluation is spent on a build identical to the start. It is folded only by the fighter-equiv dedupe; in a truncated run that eval is lost.
proposedFix: Compare the resolved preset ids (transcendencePreset(character, {transcendencePresetId})) rather than the raw field when generating moves and computing distance.
corrected: When a preset's transcendencePresetId is null, the transcendence dimension offers the 'default' preset (or whichever preset the build layer falls back to) as a move. That variant has the same board as the start state, so the evaluation is wasted. The harm is limited to a truncated search budget. The finding's mention of "distance" is not examined.
fixNotes: Resolve the current preset first, as transcendencePreset() does, and filter against the resolved id instead of the raw field. Apply the same resolution wherever the distance is computed.

title: Every sigil subset is its own kitKey group, so the screen never prunes sigils and they consume ~70% of the eva
failureScenario: Reproduced (expD/expE), with each class's whole generic pool owned. Warrior: sigils take 286 of 400 evals, pass 2 is truncated ('evals') inside the sigil step, and relics/pet/mount/glyphs/talents get one look each. Mystic Druid: 282/400; Sentinel: 286/400. The default run's best is 2.893M DPS (N=400), while maxEvals=3000 finds 2.990M (+3.3%) and is still truncated at 3000.
proposedFix: Do not let the diversity group degenerate to one group per candidate. Group sigil moves by something coarser, or evaluate sigil subsets with a successive-halving race (N=4 -> 16 -> 64) rather than a full tier-1 measure each. Give each dimension a budget share, and surface truncation prominently in the UI.
corrected: Each generic sigil subset is its own kitKey group, so the screen cannot prune the sigil dimension. With a large owned pool, sigil exhaustion takes most of the default 400-eval budget (about 70% per the finding's repro, not re-run here), and later dimensions get little or no budget. This is an accuracy trade-off, and truncation is flagged as 'evals'. | kitKey makes each sigil subset a singleton diversity group, so screenWithGroups never prunes sigil moves. The first dimension then evaluates every enumerated subset (up to 2500) against a default budget of 400 evals, which starves the later dimensions. The cost is accuracy within the budget, not an invalid state. The reported figures (about 286/400 evals, +3.3% DPS at maxEvals=3000) come from the finding and were not independently rerun.
fixNotes: Give each dimension a budget share, or screen sigil subsets with a cheap closed-form score or a successive-halving race. Alternatively, group sigil moves by a coarser key, such as which sigil swapped out. | Group sigil moves more coarsely, for example by the set of spell-kit-defining sigils only. Alternatively, cap the sigil dimension's budget share, or pre-rank subsets with the cheap screen before the group rule. Show truncation clearly in the UI.

title: Glyph pool dedupe by signature blocks socketing two identical glyphs on one mount
failureScenario: Reproduced (expF): the mount holds gl-a (g-keen, critDamage q=1) and the inventory has an identical gl-b. None of the glyph neighbours sockets gl-b next to gl-a, so a stacking +critDamage build is unreachable.
proposedFix: Dedupe only against instances that are not already socketed on this mount: build the pool per socket excluding cur, or keep up to 3 representatives per signature for minors (2 for majors).
corrected: Pool dedupe by signature, combined with the `cur.includes(id)` skip, means a second identical glyph instance can never be socketed next to an already-socketed twin. The claim is correct as stated. Whether stacking pays off is limited to minors whose secondary stat is the same; it applies to majors only where the engine stacks them (§10 says same-type majors do not stack, so majors are not affected in practice).
fixNotes: Build the pool per socket, excluding instances already in cur, and dedupe signatures only among the not-yet-socketed candidates. Equivalently, keep up to (sockets) representatives per signature for minors. For majors there is no gain, because same-type majors do not stack, so leave them deduped.

title: Utility and Ancient moves are not gated by sigil unlock level (reconcileSigils is)
failureScenario: A level-16 Necromancer with an owned BONE_SERVANT (entered by hand or via import) gets 'equip Bone Servant' suggestions. Apply then reconciles it away, so the scored build differs from the applied one.
proposedFix: Return [] from utility/ancient (and conditions) when maxSigilSlots(level, cls) === 0, matching reconcileSigils.
corrected: As stated. The 'conditions' dimension is a separate case with its own level gate (SIGIL_CONDITIONS_LEVEL), so it needs no change here.
fixNotes: In the utility and ancient moves, return [] when maxSigilSlots(character.level ?? 100, cls) === 0. Keep the existing allowance for an already-equipped species if needed.

title: Tests miss the spec-switch, level-cap and spec/duplicate-major cases; the 'every neighbour builds' test covers
failureScenario: Every defect above passes the current suite.
proposedFix: Add a property test: for every class and both specs, every neighbour is reconcile-stable (normaliseCharacter of the applied candidate equals the candidate), and no neighbour differs from its parent only by a change that leaves the fighter unchanged.
corrected: Partly right. The tests do miss the cases, and the untested spec-switch case is a live defect, not only a test gap. For MYSTIC, the talentSet neighbour switching Druid to Mage keeps the druid-only PRIMAL_AWAKENING sigil. The fighter scores it, but normaliseCharacter drops it, so the optimiser evaluates a sigil state the model would not persist. Warrior, Sentinel and Necromancer neighbours are stable. Not verified: the isolated stat effect of the sigil, whether the persisted write path drops it, and the talent-level and requiredSpec-major cases.
fixNotes: In candidates.js, the talentSet add() should run reconcileSigils-equivalent pruning on the neighbour (drop sigils not active for the new spec, or call sigil legality per spec) before returning it. Add a test to candidates.test.js that loops all classes and both specs: each neighbour must satisfy normaliseCharacter(materialise(...)) stability. Also add the Mystic Druid-to-Mage talentSet case explicitly. Keep the proposed property test from the finding, with the class loop extended to SENTINEL and NECROMANCER.

title: Survival objective ranks proxy-only 'improvements' above the current build, including against bosses that neve
failureScenario: Reproduced (scratch wb.mjs, surv.mjs). With the Warrior fixture, World Boss NONE or FORTIFIED, objective survival: ranks #1-#5 all have p = 1 and paired delta 0 ('within noise'). They swap the Arms talent set for Protection, add Basalt Guard and replace Berserk/Warborn with Defense Stance and Iron Bastion. The current preset comes 6th, and every row gets 'Apply to preset'. On chapter 1-1 the #2 result swaps War Charm (attack) for defensive relics with zero simulated effect.
proposedFix: Remove the proxy tie for survival, or put `dist` before `tie` whenever the score difference is 0, so a measured tie keeps the current build. Take 'survival' out of COMPAT for world-boss affinities that do not attack, or reject it in makeObjective. A candidate with a paired delta of exactly 0 should never rank above the baseline.
corrected: Survival ties on p are ordered by the EHP proxy before the distance from the current build. As a result, changes with no measured gain, which are the only possible outcome against non-attacking world bosses (NONE/FORTIFIED), can rank above the current build. The ranking is a deliberate design choice, so the defect is that the heuristic can outrank the baseline. I did not verify the exact positions (baseline 6th, or 12th of 12) from the reproductions. | Survival uses an EHP proxy as the tie-break ahead of dist whenever p ties. That ranks zero-measured-gain changes above the current build, and world-boss affinities that never attack (NONE; FORTIFIED per the finding) still offer survival.
fixNotes: Rank by dist before tie when the p difference is zero and the paired delta is not significant. Alternatively, drop survival from COMPAT for worldBoss, at least for NONE and FORTIFIED, or reject it in makeObjective. Keep the current build first on measured ties. | Put dist before tie when scores are equal, or rank p-ties by a simulated margin such as HP fraction left. Remove survival from COMPAT for non-attacking world-boss affinities, or reject it in makeObjective. Never rank a candidate with a paired delta of exactly 0 above the baseline.

title: PVP optimiser searches the PVE condition space, so it never offers ENEMY_HP_BELOW conditions, which are live i
failureScenario: Reproduced (scratch pvpcond.mjs). Warrior fixture vs a cloned Warrior Tank opponent: the conditions neighbours are only WARBORN_FURY MY_HP_BELOW_*, and nothing is offered for CATACLYSM. Setting CATACLYSM to ENEMY_HP_BELOW_40 moves the PVP win rate from 0.49 to 0.337 (n = 300, same seed), so the dimension is effective and the optimiser cannot explore it. A user whose best PVP build needs an execute-phase condition will never be shown it.
proposedFix: Pass the objective's combat mode into createBuildSpace (for example mode: 'pvp' when target.kind === 'pvp') and allow ENEMY_CONDITIONS in the conditions dimension for that mode. Keep the PVE filter for PVE targets.
corrected: The claim holds as stated. The PVP optimiser never proposes ENEMY_HP_BELOW_* conditions for Damage/Debuff sigils because the conditions dimension uses the PVE filter regardless of target kind. The existing PVP condition is only kept if the user already set it, so the search cannot explore a dimension that matters in PVP. | As stated. Minor nuance: nothing is wrong for PVE targets, where the filter is correct. The defect is only that PVP targets get the PVE condition space.
fixNotes: Pass a mode (pvp when target.kind === 'pvp') into createBuildSpace. In the conditions dimension, allow ENEMY_CONDITIONS when the mode is pvp and keep the SELF-only filter for PVE. Add a test that a PVP space offers ENEMY_HP_BELOW options and a PVE space does not. | Pass a mode to createBuildSpace derived from target.kind === 'pvp'. In PVP mode, allow ENEMY_CONDITIONS for Damage and Debuff sigils in the conditions dimension, and keep the SELF-only filter for PVE.

title: PVP tie-break prefers losing faster: at a 0 % win rate it recommends weaker builds (e.g. dropping the pet)
failureScenario: Reproduced (scratch pvp0.mjs). Warrior vs an opponent with 6x HP and Attack, space pet/relics/sigils: #1 'Pet: Hell Drake -> None' plus relic and sigil swaps (HP 480k, Atk 82k, mean duel 1201 ms). The baseline is ranked last at #4 (HP 557k, Atk 169k, 1681 ms). All have p = 0 and delta 0. The user is told to unequip the pet and lower Attack.
proposedFix: Make the tie depend on the outcome: among equal win rates, prefer longer duels or the opponent's lower remaining HP for losses, and shorter duels only for wins. Or drop the tie and let `dist` keep the current build.
corrected: When PVP win rates tie, the tie-break -meanMs prefers shorter duels regardless of outcome. At a 0 % win rate that ranks builds that lose faster above the current build, so the optimiser can suggest weaker builds (dropping the pet, lower Attack). It is limited to exactly tied scores and mostly affects hopeless matchups, so the impact is moderate. | Confirmed as stated. The tie-break is only sensible for wins. When the win rate is 0%, it ranks builds that lose faster ahead of the current build, and `dist` can never break the tie. The impact is on ranking and suggestions at tied scores, mainly 0%. The 100% case is fine.
fixNotes: Make the tie outcome-aware. For wins, prefer shorter duels. For losses, prefer longer duels or the opponent's lower remaining HP. A simple option is tie = p>0 ? -meanMs : +meanMs, or to use the ehpProxy/dps tier0 score as the tie when p is 0, so the current build stays first via dist. | Make the tie depend on the result. For example, use tie = -meanMs only when p is 1 (or per matchup, only for the wins). For losses, use +meanMs or the opponent's remaining HP. Alternatively, return tie 0 when p is 0 so `dist` keeps the current build. Add a test with two builds at p = 0 and different meanMs, checking that the longer-lasting or baseline one ranks first.

title: Dungeon and village-raid targets are simulated on a 100 ms tick; the game runs them on 10 ms
failureScenario: Reproduced (scratch tick.mjs, n = 200, same seeds). TTK median for dungeon_1 step 1 is 1500 ms at 100 ms vs 1000 ms at 10 ms for the Sentinel (+50 %), Necromancer 2000 vs 1910, and Warrior dungeon_3 step 8 4400 vs 4320. Attack-speed gains smaller than the 100 ms quantum are partly invisible, so dungeon/raid TTK rankings of attack-speed builds are distorted.
proposedFix: Set `t.opts = { dtMs: 10 }` for the dungeon and raid targets, cited to L1062719/L1064866. Have the engine owner add the 500 ms inter-mob gap (with minion respawn elapse) for dungeon steps.
corrected: Confirmed as stated for the 100 ms versus 10 ms tick. The quoted TTK numbers and the 500 ms inter-mob gap were not re-verified. | Dungeon and raid targets use the default 100 ms tick, but the client's dungeon and raid constants use 10 ms. The fix is to set t.opts = { dtMs: 10 } for both kinds. The 500 ms inter-mob gap is a separate engine-side gap.
fixNotes: Set t.opts = { dtMs: 10 } for the dungeon and raid targets. Check the cost and the cooldown and respawn timers at the finer tick. Add a test that dungeon and raid targets carry dtMs 10. The 500 ms inter-mob gap is a separate engine change. | In objectives.js set t.opts = { dtMs: 10 } for the dungeon and raid branches, citing L1062719 and L1064866. Expect roughly 10x the sim cost for those targets, so check the optimiser budget. Add a test that resolveTarget for dungeon and raid carries dtMs 10. Treat the 500 ms inter-mob gap with minion respawn elapse as a separate engine task.

title: Result 'changes' are compared by line index: toggling the Utility or Ancient sigil hides the real change and r
failureScenario: Reproduced (scratch changes.mjs). Warrior, ancient dimension, candidate with ancient = null: changes = ['Mount: Flameborn -> Night Wolf (level 3)', 'Major glyphs: Night Wolf (level 3) -> Warhaste Emblem (Rare)', 'Transcendence: Warhaste Emblem (Rare) -> Default (10 nodes)'], and the removed Ancient sigil is never shown. The Mystic utility dimension does the same. A glyphs-dimension candidate with minor ['gl-1', null, null] gives changes = [] ('No differences from the current preset'). Adding a utility sigil to an empty slot, a common top suggestion, misaligns the same way.
proposedFix: Diff by label, not index: build maps label -> value for both builds and report the union of labels, with 'None' for a missing one. Add minor (and mythic) glyph lines to describeBuild, or diff candidate.mountGlyphs directly.
corrected: The claim is accurate as written. Strictly, the 'invented' changes show a candidate value paired with the baseline's value for a different label. The display is wrong, but the measured score is unaffected. | The claim is accurate as written. One precision: the minor-glyph 'No differences' case only occurs when the minor swap is the sole difference from the baseline.
fixNotes: Diff by label: build a label to value map for each side and report the union of labels, using 'None' for a missing one. Add minor and mythic glyph lines to describeBuild, or diff candidate.mountGlyphs directly. Add a test where baseline and candidate differ in whether the utility or ancient sigil is set, and a minor-glyph-only swap test. | Diff by label with a Map over the union of labels, using 'None' for a missing side. Add minor and mythic glyph lines to describeBuild, or diff candidate.mountGlyphs directly. Add a regression test for utility/ancient add and remove, and for a minor-glyph swap.

title: TTK objectives rank by the median/P90 of WON fights only, so a build that loses a third of its fights outranks
failureScenario: Reproduced with scratch rank2.mjs and run1.mjs on the real Warrior L72, chapter 10 level 2, objective ttk-median, default budget. Final #1 is a talent build with value 24.5 s, but measured at N=400 it wins only 68.5% of fights. Builds ranked 10-15 win 99.5% with the same 25.0 s median and tie with it at N=400 on score (tie=0). Entry #1 also shows value 24500 with lo=25100 and hi=null, so the value sits outside its own interval. A user who applies #1 starts failing the stage about 1 time in 3.
proposedFix: Rank on a statistic that includes losses: the q-quantile of all fights with losses set to +Infinity, which equals quantile(wins, q/p) and exists when p >= q. Or make win rate the primary key and TTK the tie-break. Report a value and CI that come from the same sample set, and show the win rate on every TTK entry.
corrected: TTK median/P90 objectives rank by the quantile of won fights only. The only gate is p >= q, so a build with a 68.5% win rate can tie or beat builds with a 99.5% win rate on score. The reported value and the CI use different sample definitions (wins only vs losses as Infinity), so the value can sit outside its own interval. The scoreSamples used for the paired delta (loss = -2*cap) match neither. Severity is major. | TTK median/P90 objectives rank on the quantile of won fights only, with a win-rate threshold of just q. A build that wins about 70% of fights can outrank one that wins about 99.5%. The shown value and its CI measure different quantities (wins-only vs all-fights with losses as Infinity), so the value can fall outside its own interval. Win rate is displayed but never used in ranking.
fixNotes: Use the q-quantile over all fights with losses as +Infinity, which equals quantile(wins, q/p) and is null when p < q. Use that same value for score, display and CI. Alternatively, make win rate the primary key with TTK as the tie-break. Make the paired delta consistent with the ranking statistic, and add a test where a lower-win-rate build has the faster wins-only median. | Use the q-quantile of all fights with losses as +Infinity, which equals quantile(wins, q/p), and compute the value and CI from the same sample set. Alternatively rank by win rate first and use TTK as the tie-break. Also make the paired scoreSamples delta consistent with the ranking statistic.

title: Tier-0 screen credits the enemy's penetration to the player and ignores the player's own Penetration and the e
failureScenario: Reproduced (scratch screen.mjs). Sentinel vs FORTIFIED World Boss: screen value 99802 at Penetration 0 and 99802 at Penetration 60, while simulated DPS is 136260 vs 369778 (2.7x). Vs Oblivion floor 5 (block 20, mob pen 12) the screen is also unchanged by player penetration and credits the mob's 12 %. Penetration relics or sigil combos in large neighbour sets, such as C(n,4) relic subsets above 40, can be pruned before they are ever simulated.
proposedFix: Use `stats.totalPenetration` for p, zero the pierce term when enemy.missChance > 0, and use negate = block + miss as in §5. For PVP views, pass the opponent's block and miss and use my penetration.
corrected: The tier-0 closedFormDps screen uses enemy.penetration where the engine uses the player's stats.totalPenetration, and it ignores the target's Miss, which disables penetration. The screen cannot see the player's penetration value against blocking targets (FORTIFIED boss, Oblivion mobs, PVP). Penetration-bearing neighbours can be pruned before simulation. The PVP screen also omits pvpAttack, pvpDefense and lifesteal. This distorts candidate pruning, not final simulated results. | closedFormDps takes penetration from the enemy view instead of stats.totalPenetration, so a player's own Penetration never affects the tier-0 screen. A mob's penetration is credited to the player instead. PVP views force penetration to 0 and ignore the opponent's Miss. The enemy-Miss omission matters only for PVP opponents, because PVE mobs always have Miss 0. The PVP screen also ignores pvpAttack, pvpDefense and lifesteal (the second report; I did not verify those). Effect: against blocking targets, penetration-bearing neighbours can be pruned before simulation.
fixNotes: Use stats.totalPenetration for p. Zero the pierce term when enemy.missChance > 0. Use negate = block + miss. In the PVP views pass the opponent's block and miss, and use the player's own penetration. Update the objectives.test.js case at line 102, which currently passes penetration via the enemy. | Use `(stats.totalPenetration ?? 0) / 100` for p. Zero the pierce term when the enemy's missChance is greater than 0, and pass missChance in the PVP views. Add a test that raising totalPenetration raises closedFormDps against a target with block > 0. Optionally model the enemy-penetration threat in ehpProxy instead.

title: Wall-clock caps silently lower fidelity: finalMs shrinks the finalists' N, and maxMs/maxEvals truncate the bea
failureScenario: A PVP run with 4 finalists and spell-heavy duels at about 15 ms: finalMs 8000 gives fit = 8000 / (4 x 15) = 133, so n2 drops from 400 to 133 per matchup (CI about 1.7x wider). The ranking of finalists, which is not gated on significance, is then mostly noise. A slow device gets a different, less accurate answer for the same seed, and the beam may stop before later dimensions (talents, talentSet) are searched at all.
proposedFix: Make N and coverage the fixed contract and time the variable: drop finalMs shrinking, or make it opt-in and show it as a warning. When truncated, report which dimensions were never visited, and don't rank a non-significant finalist above the baseline.
corrected: Time-based caps (finalMs shrinking tier-2 N, and maxMs/maxEvals truncating the beam) make optimiser output device-dependent for a given seed. Truncation is reported through `truncated`, and per-entry n and CIs are shown. Two things are not disclosed: the finalMs N reduction, and which dimensions the beam never reached. This is a design trade-off that is only partly surfaced, not a correctness bug. | Wall-clock budgets make optimiser output depend on the device. The finalMs step quietly lowers the tier-2 N, with a floor of 2*n1, and the UI does not say so. Beam truncation is disclosed through `truncated` and the 'Stopped early' note, but the result does not say which dimensions were never visited. This is an undisclosed trade-off, not a silent wrong answer: per-entry n and CI are still shown.
fixNotes: Optional: show a note when finalMs reduced n2 below the budgeted value. Also list the dimensions the beam did not reach when truncated is 'time' or 'evals'. Making N fixed and time variable is a product decision, not a defect fix. | When n2 is reduced, return the requested and actual values (e.g. budget.n2Requested) and show a note like the 'Stopped early' one. When the beam is truncated, return the dimensions that were never visited and show them. Optionally, offer an effort mode that is bounded by evaluation count rather than time, so a seed gives the same result on any device.

title: tCrit95 under-states the t critical value for df 31-59 and 61-119
failureScenario: With n2 = 64 (df 63) every tier-2 DPS interval and paired delta uses 1.98 instead of 1.998, about 1 % too narrow. At df 31 the error is 2 %, so the 'significant' flag fires slightly too often near the boundary.
proposedFix: Use the upper bracket value (2.042 for 31-40, 2.021 for 41-60, 2.0 for 61-120) or an exact t quantile approximation.
corrected: tCrit95 under-states the critical value for df 31-59 (up to 2% at df 31), 61-120 (up to about 1%) and just above 120 (about 1%). df 60 is exact. Significance flags and CIs are slightly anti-conservative.
fixNotes: Use a proper t quantile approximation such as a Cornish-Fisher or Hill series. Alternatively, extend the table to cover 31-60 in steps of 5 or 10, rounding each band up to its lowest-df value.

title: Sigil-subset enumeration bypasses the screen (every subset is its own kit group) and uses up the whole PVP bud
failureScenario: Real Warrior L72 owning 12 sigils. PVE dps default: 235 of 400 tier-1 evals go to sigils, the run stops on 'evals' in pass 2, and talents get one pass of 40. PVP standard (scratch pvprun.mjs, seats both): 16 tier-1 evals in total (start plus 15 sigil subsets of 219 screened), truncated 'time', 1 pass. Relics, pet, mount, glyphs, talents, transcendence and gear set are never evaluated. With deadline=Infinity (pvp.mjs), all 120 PVP evals still went to sigils. Every PVP run for a character with 10 or more owned generic sigils therefore only ever explores sigils.
proposedFix: Group by the spell kit minus the dimension being enumerated, or cap the per-group extras globally (e.g. keep + at most perGroup groups). Better, rank sigil subsets with a cheap simulated pre-screen, or use successive halving inside the dimension. Interleave dimensions so no single one can use up the budget, and report per-dimension coverage in the result.
corrected: Sigil-subset enumeration makes every subset its own kit group, so screenWithGroups never prunes the sigils dimension. With about 10 or more owned generic sigils, that dimension spends most or all of the eval budget (120 for PVP, 400 for PVE) before the later dimensions are evaluated. The exact eval counts come from the finding's scratch runs, which I did not repeat. Severity is major, not critical, because it only limits search coverage. | Sigil-subset enumeration defeats the tier-0 screen: each subset is its own kit group and all are kept. The sigils dimension runs first, so for characters with roughly 10 or more owned generic sigils it can consume most or all of the eval or time budget (always so under the PVP budget of 120 evals and 9 s). Later dimensions get little or no exploration. The run reports itself truncated. Severity is major (a search-quality trade-off), not critical.
fixNotes: Exclude the dimension being enumerated from the group key, for example group by kit minus sigilSpecies for the sigils step. Alternatively cap the total number of groups kept, or give each dimension a share of maxEvals. | Exclude the dimension's own varying element from the group key, or cap the number of extra group survivors across the whole screen, for example keep + at most perGroup groups. Cap the evals any one dimension may use, or interleave dimensions. Add a test that a sigil dimension with 220 subsets still leaves budget for the later dimensions.

title: Builds equal in effect for the objective are deduped only by full-fighter identity: inert glyph swaps and remo
failureScenario: Real Warrior, dummy DPS, default budget: the 10 results are 5 distinct builds, each listed twice with identical value/CI/delta and differing only by a minor glyph (block 18 vs 20.7, regen 19.3 vs 16.2). Glyphs-only run (scratch minor.mjs): #2 and #3 match #1's +88,780 DPS exactly while also removing a major glyph (Ironclad Tempo or Thornmail Aegis), and #9 empties a minor socket. Half of the beam width and half of the 12 finalists go to objective-identical twins.
proposedFix: Collapse records whose per-fight score samples are identical under CRN (same seed means same samples) and keep the smallest dist. Or drop a neighbour whose tier-1 samples equal its parent's when it is more disruptive. Never list a strictly more disruptive build with an identical score.
corrected: As stated. The impact is limited to objectives where a defensive stat has no effect (dummy DPS, TTK). The search wastes beam and finalist slots on score-identical twins and can suggest needless glyph removals or swaps. | Confirmed as stated. The dedupe is by full-fighter identity only, so builds that differ only in objective-irrelevant glyph changes survive as separate beam entries, finalists and results. The exact counts in the repro (5 distinct builds each listed twice, +88,780 DPS ties) were not re-run. Impact is wasted beam and finalist slots plus misleading result rows, and the optimiser can recommend a strictly more disruptive build with the same score.
fixNotes: Collapse records with identical tier-1 sample vectors under the same seed and keep the one with the smallest dist. Alternatively, treat a neighbour whose score equals its parent's and that is more disruptive as dominated. | Add a tie collapse after scoring. When tier-1 or tier-2 score samples are identical under common random numbers (same seed), keep only the record with the smallest dist. Alternatively, drop a neighbour whose score equals its parent's when it changes more sockets. Apply it in the beam, the finalist selection and the final pool.

title: Result 'changes' omit minor-glyph socket changes, so a row says 'No differences from the current preset' next
failureScenario: Glyphs-only run on the real Warrior (minor.mjs): #1 swaps two minor glyphs (8b41.. to 7e35.., c2cd.. to 85f4..) for +88,780 DPS and `changes: []`. ResultList shows 'No differences from the current preset.', and Apply silently re-sockets glyphs.
proposedFix: Build changes from the candidate diff (candidatePatch against start), not from describe lines, or add a Minor glyphs line to describeBuild. Fail a test when a non-baseline entry has empty changes.
corrected: Minor-glyph socket changes are searched and applied but never shown. Results whose only difference is a minor glyph have empty `changes`, so the UI says 'No differences from the current preset.' | Same as the finding. Minor-glyph socket changes (and any change among equal-looking instances) are missing from result.changes, so a minor-only candidate shows 'No differences from the current preset' even though Apply changes the sockets.
