fixNotes: Store a hash of the build inputs when the sheet is saved. In computePresetStats, compare it with the current inputs. If they differ, skip the overlay and the residual and show a "sheet out of date" warning. As a smaller step, have applyCandidate offer to clear the sheet or re-enter it, and show a stale banner on the Presets and Optimiser screens. | Store a fingerprint of the build inputs (or a changed flag) when the sheet is saved. In computePresetStats, if it differs, show a visible 'sheet is stale' warning, and optionally skip the overlay and the residual. Alternatively have applyCandidate flag or clear the sheet, or prompt the user to re-enter it. The other duplicate reports (residual carried across equipmentSet/talentSet candidates, and residual added on the total instead of rescaled for Attack%/HP%) are separate and lesser: the second is plausible but moderate, and the third is minor and acknowledged in the UI caveat.

title: describeBuild emits a variable set of lines, so the optimiser's index-based change list is misaligned
failureScenario: Reproduced (scratch exp8.mjs). The Warrior fixture candidate only removes the Ancient sigil. The change list shows 'Mount: Flameborn -> Night Wolf (level 3)', 'Major glyphs: Night Wolf (level 3) -> Warhaste Emblem (Rare)' and 'Transcendence: Warhaste Emblem (Rare) -> Default (10 nodes)'. The real change (Ancient sigil removed) is never shown. Adding or removing a utility sigil does the same.
proposedFix: Make describeBuild always emit the same labels in the same order ('None' when empty), and have search.js diff by label rather than by index.
corrected: The claim holds as written. The effect is limited to the displayed change list: the candidate evaluation itself is unaffected. The misalignment shows up only when a candidate differs from the baseline in whether a utility or ancient sigil is set. | Claim holds as stated. The harm is limited to the displayed change list and `lines`; scoring is unaffected. Removing the ancient sigil gives wrong 'Mount/Major glyphs/Transcendence' diffs and hides the removal.
fixNotes: Make describeBuild always emit the Utility and Ancient sigil lines, with 'None' when empty. Or diff by label in search.js, treating a missing label as 'None'. | Diff by label (Map keyed by label, with a missing label counting as None), or make describeBuild always emit the Utility sigil and Ancient sigil lines with NONE. Add a test where a candidate drops the ancient sigil.

title: describeBuild omits minor glyphs, so a socket-only recommendation shows no changes
failureScenario: Reproduced (scratch exp2.mjs). A candidate that only swaps a minor socket to a Legendary Attack% glyph raises totalAttack from 169344 to 179268 (+5.9%). Its describe diff is [], so the result row shows a gain with no visible change, and a user copying the build into the game misses the glyph swap.
proposedFix: Add a 'Minor glyphs' line (type, rarity and secondary stat/value for each socket), and a mythic line for completeness.
corrected: describeBuild omits minor (and mythic) glyph sockets. A search candidate that only changes a minor glyph has an empty 'changes' list even though its score differs. Severity is better described as a completeness/UX gap in the recommendation output than a game-math error. | describeBuild lists only major glyphs. Minor-glyph swaps, which the optimiser's glyphs dimension generates, appear in neither lines nor changes, so a minor-only recommendation shows a score gain with an empty change list. Mythic sockets are also omitted, but the optimiser does not vary them (the glyph neighbours cover only minor and major tiers).
fixNotes: Add a 'Minor glyphs' line built from the loadout's minors (type, rarity, secondary stat and value). Optionally add a mythic line. Add a test covering a socket-only candidate that produces a non-empty change. | Add a 'Minor glyphs' line to describeBuild, built from loadout.minors with type, rarity and secondary stat/value. Add a mythic line only for display. Lines are diffed by index and label, so keep the line order consistent between baseline and candidate. Add a test where only a minor socket differs and the result has a non-empty changes list.

title: Drop Check builds PVP opponents with its own opponentFighter that drops the Druid form, skips the major-glyph
failureScenario: Reproduced (scratchpad audit/features-rules/druid.mjs). The saved opponent is a MYSTIC_DRUID with utility DIRE_URSINE and sigils PRIMAL_INSTINCT, ARCANE_BURST and RUNIC_AFFLICTION, using the real L72 computedStats. Against a Warrior at 1.5x attack, Drop Check's fighter gives a win rate of 0.280 and the Duel screen's gives 0.200. With ALPHA_LUPINE it is 0.280 vs 0.185. Drop Check therefore reports a different PVP before/after, and possibly a different verdict, for the same opponent than the Duel screen. A brand-new opponent (sheet.values = {}) is also offered and simulated (see the missingStats finding). The missing glyph filter is inert today only because the engine self-gates per species: 0 of 42 glyphs changed a duel in opp4.mjs.
proposedFix: Delete swap.js opponentFighter. DropCheckScreen should import features/duel.js opponentFighter and filter out opponents where missingStats(f).length > 0. Add a swap/dropCheck test with a Druid opponent.
corrected: Drop Check's opponentFighter (swap.js) omits the Druid form (formKind/formConfig), so MYSTIC_DRUID opponents with a FORM utility sigil are simulated formless and win rates differ from the Duel screen and optimiser. The missing major-glyph sigil filter is inert today, and empty-sheet opponents are accepted (the missingStats gap). | Drop Check's swap.js opponentFighter drops the Druid form (formConfig/formKind), so Druid opponents with a FORM utility sigil are simulated formless and disagree with the Duel screen and optimiser. It also accepts opponents with empty or incomplete sheets, and does not normalise the opponent or filter major glyphs by equipped sigil. The glyph filter is inert in practice.
fixNotes: Delete the swap.js opponentFighter and use features/duel.js opponentFighter in DropCheckScreen. Filter out opponents where missingStats(f).length > 0. Add a Druid-opponent test in swap/dropCheck tests, and update swap.test.js:179 and dropCheck.test.js:55 to import the duel.js function. | Delete swap.js opponentFighter. Have DropCheckScreen use duel.js opponentFighter and filter out opponents where missingStats(f).length > 0. Add a Drop Check test with a Druid opponent.

title: PVP win-rate delta at N=64 is badly underpowered, and an unresolved result is labelled 'Sidegrade'
failureScenario: User enables PVP vs an opponent and tests a +3% attack ring worth +1.8 pts. 86% of the time the card says 'Sidegrade' with a +-10 pt interval, which reads as 'no effect'.
proposedFix: Raise N_PVP/nPvp (N=1000 costs ~1.5 s per opponent and halves the CI roughly 4x), or add a 'inconclusive' verdict state when the CI half-width exceeds the minimum interesting size (NEUTRAL_PROB) instead of calling it sidegrade.
corrected: With PVP enabled, the Drop Check uses N=64 duels per opponent. The paired win-rate interval is about +-5-10 pts wide, so real +1-3 pt changes are usually not detected. A not-detected result is then labelled 'Sidegrade' because no inconclusive state exists. This is a labelling and power issue in an opt-in metric. It is not an engine/client mismatch. | With PVP enabled, Drop Check's default N=64 gives a paired win-rate interval about +-10 points wide. Real effects of 0.5-3 points are therefore almost always reported as 'Sidegrade', because 'no significant difference' and 'inconclusive' share one verdict state. This is an underpowered, mislabelled-by-omission verdict, not a computation error. The power figures were reported but not re-measured here.
fixNotes: Add an 'inconclusive' verdict or note when the CI half-width exceeds NEUTRAL_PROB, or let the user raise N_PVP. Raising N is cheap per the finding (about 1.5 ms per duel). | Add an 'inconclusive' signal when the interval half-width exceeds NEUTRAL_PROB, and/or raise N_PVP, perhaps with an adaptive or optional higher-N pass. Keep 'sidegrade' for intervals that are narrow and centred near 0. Downgrade the severity to minor/moderate.

title: missingStats only requires HP and Attack; an opponent sheet missing Crit Damage or HP Regen yields NaN HP and
failureScenario: Reproduced (nan.mjs, nan2.mjs). Take an opponent with the full real L72 sheet but no totalCritDamage, or no totalHpRegen. missingStats is [], so the Duel screen runs. runDuel then returns defenderHpLeft NaN and ends at 600-2250 ms. pvpWinRate is p = 0 whichever seat my preset takes. In Drop Check (empty.mjs), a new opponent ({} sheet), or one typed only with HP/Atk/AS/Crit, gives before 0 and after 0 even when the candidate doubles Attack, so the verdict is 'sidegrade'. The optimiser's PVP objective (pvpObjective.js:62 uses missingStats as its gate) scores every candidate 0 and picks arbitrarily.
proposedFix: Make every stat the resolver reads arithmetically required: at least totalCritDamage and totalHpRegen. Or fill absent keys with explicit neutral defaults (critDamage 1, regen 0) before building the fighter, and say in the UI which stats were defaulted. Add an engine assert that rejects non-finite HP at duel end instead of declaring a winner.
corrected: As stated. The impact is a premature, invalid duel result (NaN HP, or an end at about 1s) rather than always NaN. The Drop Check and 0% win-rate consequences were not independently re-run. | The claim holds, and it is broader than stated. Any stat the resolver reads that is absent from an opponent sheet (Crit Damage and HP Regen, but also Attack Speed, Crit Chance and others) passes the HP and Attack gate and gives NaN or undefined in the duel. The result is a silently wrong win rate and an arbitrary pick in the PVP optimiser and Drop Check. A real server profile always has every key, so the trigger is a partial manual or blank-sheet opponent entry.</Annotation>
fixNotes: Add every stat the resolver reads without a default to the required list. At minimum that means totalCritDamage, totalHpRegen, totalAttackSpeed and the chance and reduction stats, or fill neutral defaults and tell the user which were defaulted. Also make the engine reject non-finite HP at duel end. | Require the full set of resolver-read stats in missingStats, or fill neutral defaults for absent keys (critDamage 1, regen 0, and so on) and tell the user which were defaulted. Also add a finite-HP assert at duel end.

title: Oblivion floor scan uses a 5-minute fight cap (maxMs 300000), not the client engine's 20-minute cap, and stops
failureScenario: Reproduced (obl.mjs). The fighter is the real L72 Warrior sheet with attack x2, HP x3 and Oblivion Power 2000 (strain 0). Floors 26/28/30 give p = 0 at 300 s and p = 1 at 1 200 s (median fight 370-604 s). The task reports maxFloor 24 and stops at floor 27. Under the engine's own cap the fighter clears all 30. Sustain-heavy Oblivion builds facing 400M-700M HP floor mobs see 'max floor' understated.
proposedFix: Default maxMs to the engine's FIGHT_CAP_MS (import it rather than hard-coding a number). Report timeouts separately from deaths, and do not count timeouts toward stopAfter. Treat the server's cap as [UNRESOLVED] in the UI.

title: Batch drop ranking takes the best single preset and ignores that applying the item changes the whole set (sing
failureScenario: Reproduced (judge.mjs). Presets A and B both use set1. The item gives A +6% DPS and B -9%. The batch list ranks it 'upgrade' at the top. Loaded into the single view, set1's aggregate verdict is 'mixed'. A user acting on the ranked list equips a net downgrade for preset B.
proposedFix: Judge per set with aggregateVerdict over that set's rows (as the single view does), take the best set, and rank by that. Show the per-set verdict in the list.
corrected: Batch drop ranking judges per preset rather than per equipment set. When presets sharing a set disagree, the item is ranked "upgrade" although equipping it into that set is "mixed" (as the single view shows). This is a misleading ranking with minor severity, because Apply only happens in the single view. | Batch ranking judges each item by its single best preset row, not by per-set aggregate. An item that helps one preset and hurts another on the same equipment set ranks as 'upgrade' in the batch list, but the single view shows 'mixed' for that set. This is a ranking-accuracy and consistency issue, partly disclosed in the UI ('best of N presets'), and not a legality bug: the batch list applies nothing.
fixNotes: Group rows by setKey, apply aggregateVerdict per set, take the best set, and rank on that. Show the per-set verdict in the list. | Group rows by setKey, apply aggregateVerdict per set, and take the best set as the entry's verdict. Show the per-set verdict, and the 'upgrades' count that is already computed, in BatchList. Alternatively, keep the best-preset rule and label it explicitly as 'may be mixed on its set'.

title: Oblivion-realm Drop Check anchors every preset to the single oblivion.sheet, so non-active presets are judged
failureScenario: The character has the rift unlocked and an oblivion.sheet imported while preset P1 (pet X, talent set 0) was active, and also has P2 (pet Y, talent set 1). An Oblivion drop is checked. P2's row shows before stats identical to P1's sheet, with P1's pet and talent bonuses, and its anchored after and verdict build on that. P2's real Oblivion stats are never used.
proposedFix: Anchor to oblivion.sheet only for the preset that was active when it was captured; record that preset id on the sheet. Other presets fall back to the computed tier 1, or carry the residual (tier 3).
corrected: In the Oblivion realm, Drop Check anchors every preset to the one oblivion.sheet, which was captured under whichever preset was active. Non-active presets therefore show that preset's stats as their baseline, including its pet, talent and sigil bonuses, instead of their own. Only Oblivion Drop Check with an imported sheet and multiple presets is affected.
fixNotes: Store the capturing preset id on oblivion.sheet and anchor only that preset to it. Other presets would use computed tier 1, or computed stats plus a residual taken from the active preset. Alternatively, warn in the UI that the other presets' Oblivion rows are approximate.

title: Drop items accept any conduit type for a rarity and realm that allow a conduit (e.g. a base-realm Eternal with
failureScenario: In Drop Check the user enters a base-realm ETERNAL item with a DARK conduit, or an Oblivion-realm DIVINE item with FLAME. The item is accepted, itemRawDelta credits totalDarkConduit / totalFlameConduit, and the sim charges Chrono Flux on a conduit the game cannot roll.
proposedFix: Validate the conduit type against rarity and realm per rollConduitForRarity, and drop or flag an impossible type.
corrected: Conduit type is not validated against what rarity and realm can roll. A base-realm Eternal with DARK, or an Oblivion-realm Divine+ item with FLAME or EARTHEN, normalises as valid. The game would roll FLAME or EARTHEN for the first and DARK for the second. Low impact: the user enters the data by hand, and per the doc the conduit's combat effect is [UNRESOLVED] and not modelled.
fixNotes: Add a conduitTypesFor(rarity, realm) helper: oblivion realm and rarity >= DIVINE gives DARK, ETERNAL gives FLAME/EARTHEN, Oblivion rarity gives DARK. Check c.type against it, and leave unknown rarity permissive. Add tests.

title: Drop Check / batch verdict is decided by training-dummy DPS only; HP%, DR, lifesteal, regen, block and penetration items read 'Sidegrade'
failureScenario: User imports a loot bag. A +HP%/+DR helm that is worth +20 pts of PVP win rate ranks below every +0.3% DPS item and is labelled 'Sidegrade'. An item that trades HP for attack is shown 'Upgrade' (DPS up, nothing else measured), with a green 'Apply' button.
proposedFix: Make the verdict state which metrics it covers (e.g. 'DPS only, defence not measured') when survival/PVP are off, or default PVP/survival on when the item changes defensive keys (statDeltas shows HP/DR/etc.). In dropBatch, include survival or PVP vs saved opponents, or flag items whose statDeltas touch non-DPS keys as 'not judged by DPS'.
corrected: By default, and always in batch mode, the Drop Check verdict is judged on sim DPS alone against a training dummy. Items whose benefit is defensive (HP%, DR, lifesteal, regen, block, penetration) read 'Sidegrade'. Items that trade defence for attack read 'Upgrade'. Nothing tells the user the defensive axes were not measured. Survival and PVP signals only enter the verdict if the user opts in on the single-item screen. | By default, and always in batch mode, the Drop Check verdict covers training-dummy DPS only. Items whose effect is defensive (HP%, DR, lifesteal, regen, block) are labelled 'Sidegrade', and HP-for-attack trades are labelled 'Upgrade', with no indication that defence was not evaluated. Survival and PVP signals exist but are opt-in, and batch has no way to enable them. This is a labelling and UX gap in a DPS-focused design, not an engine/client mismatch.
fixNotes: The cheapest fix is a label. Show "DPS only, defence not measured" on the verdict when survival and PVP are off, or when the item's stat deltas touch non-DPS keys. Alternatives: default survival on when defensive keys change, or add a survival signal to the batch request. | Show 'DPS only, defence not measured' next to the verdict when survival and PVP are off. Flag items whose statDeltas touch non-DPS keys as 'not judged by DPS' in the single check and the batch. Optionally let batch include survival or PVP against saved opponents.

title: Zero-discordant-pair paired deltas show a zero-width '95% CI' that excludes the true effect
failureScenario: Card prints 'PVP vs Rogue 52% -> 52%, +0.0 pts, 95% CI 0.0 to 0.0 pts' for an item worth +1 pt. The user takes it as measured-exactly-zero.
proposedFix: For binary paired samples use an exact/score interval on the discordant pairs (McNemar/Newcombe-Wilson), or at minimum widen the degenerate case (add a 0.5 pseudo-count or print 'no outcome changed in N duels').
corrected: pairedDelta applies a t interval to paired 0/1 outcomes. When no outcome changes, or very few do, the interval collapses to [0,0] or is far too narrow, and VerdictCard shows "95% CI 0.0 to 0.0 pts" for a win-rate delta. This understates uncertainty (about ±5 pts at N=64). It affects display only, since the significance flag stays false. | pairedDelta on 0/1 samples (PVP and survival) uses a t interval. With zero or few discordant pairs it yields a degenerate or undercovering interval, and the UI shows "95% CI 0.0 to 0.0 pts". The flaw is a misleading display and undercoverage, not a wrong verdict, because `significant` correctly stays false.
fixNotes: For binary deltas, use an exact or score interval on the discordant pairs (McNemar or Newcombe), or a Wilson-style interval on the paired difference. At minimum, when sd===0 on 0/1 data, show "no outcome changed in N duels" instead of the numeric CI. | For binary paired samples, use an interval based on the discordant-pair counts (Newcombe or Wilson on the paired difference, or an exact McNemar-style bound). At minimum, when sd===0 with 0/1 data, print "no outcome changed in N duels" instead of a numeric CI, or widen the interval using the rule of three.

title: Verdict combines up to 2+K independent 95% tests with 'any up and none down' and no multiplicity control; best-of-presets adds more
failureScenario: A cosmetic swap checked against 5 saved opponents gets a green 'Upgrade' about 1 time in 8 purely from noise. The same item is a spurious 'Downgrade' or 'Mixed' (confirm-click) about 1 in 8 / 1 in 50 times.
proposedFix: Apply a correction (Bonferroni/Holm on the family of PVP+survival tests) or require lo > 0 on the pooled/average PVP delta rather than any single opponent; show per-opponent results as informational.
corrected: The verdict ORs up to 2+K independent per-test 95% intervals with no multiplicity control, so a swap whose true effect is near zero but whose fights are not identical gets a spurious non-sidegrade verdict far more often than 5% (about 26% with 6 tests), and best-of-presets inflates it further. A pure no-op swap is not affected, because common random numbers give identical samples and a zero-width interval. | The verdict ORs 2+K independent 95% paired tests with no multiplicity correction, and judgeEntry takes the best over presets. This inflates false 'upgrade', 'downgrade' and 'mixed' verdicts for items whose true effect is near zero but not exactly zero, because common random numbers make an exactly identical or cosmetic swap give delta 0. The 26% non-sidegrade rate with 6 tests is an upper bound for near-null items, not for items with no effect at all.
fixNotes: Apply Holm or Bonferroni across the survival and PVP tests, or require lo>0 on a pooled PVP delta before it can set the verdict. Alternatively, raise the neutral floor for PVP win-rate to a few percentage points. Show per-opponent signals as informational only. | Use Holm or Bonferroni across the PVP and survival tests, or base the verdict on the pooled or average PVP delta. Show per-opponent results as informational only. For best-of-presets, either show the count of presets that upgrade (already tracked as `upgrades`) or require the CI to hold after correction. Add a test that runs near-null items and checks the false-upgrade rate.

title: 60 s DPS window front-loads cooldowns and under-weights slow stacking; absolute DPS is 9-10% low and attack-speed value is overstated up to 50%
failureScenario: Comparing a speed roll with a crit roll on a spec with long-cycle stacks: the 60 s window ranks speed about 30-50% higher than the steady state does, so the 'better' item can flip.
proposedFix: Report steady-state DPS (warm-up discarded or 180-300 s), or make seconds a user setting and state the window next to the number; at minimum label it 'first 60 s'.

title: Oblivion screen keeps old floor-scan results after gear/character changes
failureScenario: User scans (maxFloor 20), swaps in a weaker Oblivion weapon on the same screen, and still reads 'Highest floor at 90%+: 20' next to the new, lower Power.
proposedFix: Key results to a hash of (character id, active preset, equipment.oblivion, relevant stats) like DropCheckScreen's gearSig/batchStale; clear or grey them when it changes, and ignore a scan that finishes for a different key.
corrected: Oblivion floor-scan results are not invalidated when the character, preset or Oblivion gear changes, or when a scan finishes after a character switch. Win % and 'Highest floor at 90%+' can disagree with the live Power and strain columns until the user rescans. The effect is stale display only. Severity is minor, not major. | Confirmed as described, but the severity is minor: stale scan results remain displayed after gear, preset, stat or character changes, with no staleness indicator. A scan in flight when the character changes also writes the old character's rows into the new character's view. This is a UI-robustness gap, not an engine error.
fixNotes: Store a signature (character id, active preset id, oblivion equipment and level, stats.totalOblivionPower) alongside `results`. Compare it to the current signature and grey out or clear the results on mismatch. In scan(), capture the signature at start and discard the output if it differs on completion. Cancel the scan on character switch. | Compute a signature of the scan inputs: character id, active preset id, equipment.oblivion and the relevant stats, or simply the `fighter` that runFloorScan builds. Store it alongside `results` when a scan starts. On completion, discard the output if the signature has changed since the scan started. In the template, grey out the results and show a 'stale' hint when the stored signature differs from the current one, as DropCheckScreen does with gearSig/batchStale. Alternatively, clear `results` and cancel the scan in an $effect on the character id and signature.

title: Oblivion floor win % / 'highest floor at 90%' presented as game fact although floor resolution is [SERVER]
failureScenario: User spends keys/stones to push a floor the screen called 90%+, but the server's fight differs; or a strong character is told its best is 30 only because the scan stops there.
proposedFix: Label the table 'model estimate (server resolves the real fight)', drop or relabel '95% range' as 'sampling range', and show 'cap reached' when floor FLOOR_COUNT passes the threshold (scan beyond 30 or until two failures).
corrected: The Oblivion floor table and the "Highest floor at 90%+" readout show a local client-rule simulation with no model caveat, although the server resolves the real fight [SERVER] and where the damage and defence multipliers apply is [UNRESOLVED]. "95% range" reflects only sampling noise. Floor 30 also acts as a silent cap on the highest-floor readout. This is a labelling and UX gap rather than an engine bug, so it is minor. | The Oblivion floor table and "Highest floor at 90%+" present the shared-PVE-tick simulation without saying the real floor fight is resolved server-side and is not fully modelled. The "95% range" column shows only sampling noise. The scan stops at floor 30 and gives no cap indicator. Severity is minor (UI labelling), not major.
fixNotes: Add a caption or tooltip such as "model estimate - the server resolves the real fight". Rename "95% range" to "sampling range". Show "30+ (scan cap)" when floor 30 passes the threshold, or extend the scan until two consecutive failures. | Add a hint such as "Model estimate; the server resolves the real fight". Relabel "95% range" as "sampling range". Show "30+ (scan cap)" when floor 30 passes the threshold.

title: fromMySide turns a zero-sample summary (n=0 or cancelled before the first duel) into a 100% win rate for the defender seat
failureScenario: User sits on the defender seat, hits Cancel on the first tick: the result panel shows a 100% [100%-100%] win rate.
proposedFix: Return the summary unchanged when summary.p == null or n === 0; have DuelScreen hide the result when n === 0.

title: No tests for the oblivionFloors task, oblivionDungeon.js helpers, the Worker branch of the client, optimizerWorker.js, or the null/zero-sample paths
failureScenario: Regressions in the worker message protocol (progress/done/error/abort) or in the floor-scan stopping rule reach users unnoticed.
proposedFix: Add a fake-Worker test for runInWorker (progress, done, error, cancel-before-start), a unit test for oblivionFloors (stopAfter, abort, n=0, maxFloor) and for the helpers, and edge tests for fromMySide/signalOf.
corrected: oblivionFloors scan logic, runInWorker, and optimizerWorker.js have no direct tests; oblivionDungeon helpers and signalOf/fromMySide have partial coverage.
fixNotes: Add a fake-Worker test for runInWorker, oblivionFloors tests for stopAfter/abort/n=0/non-contiguous maxFloor, and edge tests for the helpers.

title: Worker is spawned per request: construction errors escape, and the metrics memo cache never survives a run in the browser
failureScenario: A browser/CSP that rejects module workers makes Drop Check show 'Simulating...' indefinitely with no error text; re-running an unchanged request pays the full cost again.
proposedFix: Wrap `new Worker` in try/catch and fall back to the inline path (or reject), and either keep one long-lived worker or correct the metrics.js header to say the cache is per-request in the browser.
corrected: Confirmed as described, with low likelihood. A synchronous Worker constructor throw (for example SecurityError) leaves Drop Check stuck on 'running'. The metrics memo cache is per-request in the browser because each worker is terminated. Async worker failures are already handled via onerror.
fixNotes: Wrap new Worker in try/catch and fall back to the inline runTask path. Alternatively, return a rejected promise. Wrap the runOptimizerTask call in the DropCheckScreen setTimeout in try/catch so status becomes 'error'. Correct the metrics.js header note, or keep one long-lived worker.

title: Pet secondaries are clamped and re-quantised to a v1 'observed' envelope, so imported real rolls are silently altered
failureScenario: Repro (scratch t1.mjs): a profile pet with secondaryStats HEALTH_PERCENT 24.3, SPELL_DAMAGE 2.1 and CRIT_DAMAGE 0.175 imports as 22.6, 2.6 and 18. A legitimate server roll above the highest value seen in the v1 sample (HEALTH_PERCENT 22.6, ATTACK_SPEED 32.0 = 0.32, ATTACK_PERCENT 21.0, ...) or below its lowest is moved. The import is meant to be exact. The equipped pet's contribution then differs from computedStats, and the tier-3 residual is absorbed into baseResidual or every candidate.
proposedFix: Do not clamp pet secondaries to the observed envelope in normalisation. Keep only type validity, the finite and >=0 check, the slot cap and the class gate. Move the envelope to UI-only slider hints. Round to a fixed number of decimals (e.g. 3), not to a step grid.
corrected: Pet secondaries, including values imported from a real game profile, are clamped to the v1-observed min/max and re-quantised to a step. The docs say real roll ranges are [SERVER] and unknown. Rolls outside the observed envelope or finer than the step are therefore altered on import, so the pet stats the app computes can differ from what the game applied. The effect on baseResidual and on non-active presets is plausible but was not verified. | Pet secondary values are hard-clamped to a v1-observed min/max and re-quantised to a step grid in normalisePets, including on game-profile import. Out-of-envelope or finer-grained real server rolls are silently changed. The real fixture's only pet is unaffected, so the impact is latent, but the game has no such range ([SERVER]).
fixNotes: Normalisation should enforce only type validity, finite and >=0, the slot cap and the class gate, and round to about 3 decimals. The envelope should stay as UI slider hints only, and the clamp should be applied in the editor, not in normalisePets. Check src/lib/store/pets.js and pets.test.js for callers that rely on the clamp. | In normaliseSecondaries, validate type, finiteness, >=0, slot cap and class gate, and round to 3 decimals. Keep PET_SECONDARY_RANGES as slider hints in PetCard.svelte and the store only. Callers of clampSecondaryValue (store/pets.js, PetCard.svelte) can keep clamping for manual entry.

title: Imported build presets are left unlinked from the active Transcendence preset, so the build falls back to 'default' and drops the live bonuses
failureScenario: Repro (t1.mjs T2): a profile with transcendencePresets [default (empty), x (20 nodes)] and activeTranscendencePresetId 'x' imports with both presets' transcendencePresetId = null. buildPresetInputs gives transcendence attackPercent 0 and hp 0, while the sheet includes x. Tier-3 validation shows a large phantom residual. 'Absorb into base' or the carried residual then bakes the missing Transcendence into the base. The optimiser's 'transcendence' dimension compares against a wrong baseline.
proposedFix: In the importer, resolve null links to profile.activeTranscendencePresetId (at least for the active build preset). Alternatively have transcendencePreset() fall back to character.transcendence.activePresetId before 'default'.
corrected: When a game profile is imported and the active Transcendence preset is not 'default', build presets with a null transcendencePresetId are computed against the 'default' board instead of the active one. The game most likely plays an unlinked build preset on the active Transcendence preset, since stats come from the active board, but docs/Reference/Game/transcendence.md does not state this as [CODE]. The mismatch shows up as a residual and a wrong optimiser baseline. It is limited to profiles with a non-default active preset, so it is minor-to-major rather than clearly major. | An unlinked build preset (transcendencePresetId null), whether imported or native, is evaluated against the 'default' Transcendence board. The client's live board is the active Transcendence preset, whose nodes are written into transcendenceNodes. The importer discards activeTranscendencePresetId, and character.transcendence.activePresetId has no consumer in build or engine. So stats, residual and optimiser baseline are wrong whenever the active preset differs from 'default'. Whether the server uses the active preset for computedStats is inferred from the client store, not shown directly.
fixNotes: In gameProfile.js, resolve a null build-preset link to profile.activeTranscendencePresetId on import. At minimum do this for the active build preset, and it is safer for all of them. Alternatively, make transcendencePreset() fall back to character.transcendence.activePresetId before 'default'. The second option also changes behaviour for native, non-imported characters, so check data-model.md first. Add a test with an imported profile whose active Transcendence preset is not 'default'. | Simplest fix is to have transcendencePreset() fall back to character.transcendence.activePresetId before 'default'. That covers native users too. Alternatively the importer can set null links to profile.activeTranscendencePresetId, at least for the active build preset. Add a test with an active non-default preset and an unlinked build preset.

title: computedStats is always attached to the active preset even when the live loadout differs from it (dirty state)
failureScenario: Repro (t1.mjs T3): the active preset says equipmentSet 1, but the player switched to set 2 (or swapped the pet or relics) without saving. The sheet for set 2 is stored on the preset that references set 1. engines use the sheet verbatim, diffSheet reports bogus residuals against the wrong gear, and 'absorb' or the carried residual contaminates every candidate for that preset. The fixture hides this because its live state equals preset 'default'.
proposedFix: Compare the live selections with the active preset. If they differ, build an extra 'Live' preset from the live state (as implicitPreset does) and attach the sheet to it, or drop the sheet. Add a test with activeEquipmentSet 2 against a preset on set 1.
corrected: On import, computedStats (the server total for the live loadout, which is [SERVER]-derived) is attached to the active preset even when the live selections differ from that preset (dirty state). The sheet then describes different gear, pet, mount, relics or sigils than the preset references. Severity is major only for dirty profiles, which is a real and reachable state; clean profiles are unaffected. | When a profile has presets and the live loadout differs from the active preset (unsaved changes), the server's `computedStats` sheet is still attached to the active preset. The sheet then describes the live state rather than that preset's references. The proposed fix is sound: detect the mismatch and either add a Live preset or drop the sheet.
fixNotes: Compare the live selections with the active preset. If they differ, either add an extra 'Live' preset built from the live state (as implicitPreset does) and attach the sheet to it, or drop the sheet. Add a test with activeEquipmentSet 2 against a preset on set 1. | In `mapPresets`, compare each live field with the active preset: `equipmentSet`, `talentSet`, `petId`, `mountId`, `relicIds` as a set, and the sigil lists. If any differ, append an extra 'Live' preset built by `implicitPreset` (it counts against `MAX_PRESETS`) and attach the sheet to it, or set the sheet to null. Add a test with `activeEquipmentSet: 2` against a preset on set 1.

title: Relic slot count is not modelled: every preset may equip 4 relics regardless of purchased slots
failureScenario: A player with 2 or 3 slots imports (relicIds length 2, extra=0). The app lets the user equip 4 relics, and the optimiser proposes 4-relic builds (default relicSlots 4) that the game cannot equip. It over-reports the achievable stats. Repro (t1.mjs T5): extraSlotsPurchased 0 is discarded and the 4 relic ids are kept.
proposedFix: Persist relics.extraSlots (0..2) or a derived relic slot count. Import extraSlotsPurchased, cap preset.relicIds at 2 + extra in normalise/reconcile, and use it as the optimiser's relicSlots upper bound.
corrected: The app does not track purchased relic slots (2 base + up to 2 purchased, per the client). All preset, UI and optimiser limits assume 4. A player with 2 or 3 slots can equip 4 relics, and the optimiser defaults to 4-relic builds. The game would not allow the extra relics, so the optimiser can over-report achievable stats. Impact is moderate: the user can reduce the optimiser's relicSlots manually, and the import only brings in the relics that were really equipped. | The app has no model of relic slots bought. Every preset and the optimiser default allow 4 relics, and gameProfile import drops extraSlotsPurchased. For players with 2 or 3 slots, the app accepts and suggests relic loadouts the game cannot equip. The user can work around it by choosing fewer relics or lowering the optimiser relicSlots, so the practical impact is minor.
fixNotes: Add a character-wide relics.extraSlots (0..2) and import extraSlotsPurchased from the game profile. Use 2 + extra as the cap in normalise, reconcile, the store's equip action, the PresetEditor and RelicsScreen UI, and the optimiser's relicSlots default and clamp. Default existing saves to 2 (the current behaviour) so nothing is silently dropped. | Add a character-wide relics.extraSlots (0-2), import it from relicState.extraSlotsPurchased, and use 2 + extra as the cap in the preset relicIds normaliser, the store mutators, the PresetEditor and the optimiser relicSlots upper bound. Document it in data-model.md. Default it to 2 for old saves so existing builds are not truncated.

title: Mystic Druid profile without build presets imports the Mage sigil arrays instead of the live Druid ones
failureScenario: Repro (t2.mjs): a MYSTIC with Druid talents, no presets, druidEquippedSpecies [ARCANE_SHARD, ARCANE_EMPOWERMENT, PRIMAL_AWAKENING] and druidUtilitySlotSpecies DIRE_URSINE imports with the Mage list and utility ARCANE_BARRIER. reconcileSigils then drops the Shield utility and the Druid-only picks, so utilitySigilSpecies = null. The Form sigil is lost, so formConfig is null and the bear/wolf multipliers (gearHpMult 1.6 etc.) are missing from the whole computed build.
proposedFix: In implicitPreset (and in mapPresetSigils when preset lists are absent or empty), choose the Druid arrays when the active talent set's specialization is MYSTIC_DRUID. It would also help to record which array client presets snapshot for Druid.
corrected: As stated. Scope: only the no-presets path. mapPresetSigils for client presets is a separate question the finding only touches in passing (which array a client preset snapshots for a Druid is unverified). The fix needs the active talent set's specialization, which is available in the profile. | For a Mystic Druid profile with no presets, implicitPreset ignores druidEquippedSpecies and druidUtilitySlotSpecies and imports the Mage arrays. The Druid generic sigils and Form sigil are then dropped or replaced. The same gap would apply to mapPresetSigils if client presets snapshot the Druid arrays; that is unverified.
fixNotes: In implicitPreset, pick sigils.druidEquippedSpecies and sigils.druidUtilitySlotSpecies when profile.class is MYSTIC and the active talent set's specialization is MYSTIC_DRUID. Otherwise keep the generic arrays. Add a test with a Druid profile that has no presets. | In implicitPreset, pick the druid* arrays when the active talent set's spec is MYSTIC_DRUID. Add a test with a Druid profile that has no presets.

title: Equipped relics need not be owned: reconcile only checks the class, so unowned relics stay equipped and are inert
failureScenario: Repro (t3.mjs R1): relics = {} with 4 relicIds in the preset normalises with the 4 ids intact. The preset shows 4 equipped relics, takes 0 stats from them and uses up all 4 slots. This also happens after the user sets a relic to level 0.
proposedFix: In reconcileRelics, drop ids with (character.relics?.[id] ?? 0) <= 0. Run the reconcile from setRelicLevel.
corrected: Equipped relics are not checked for ownership by reconcileRelics or toggleRelic. The state is reachable via setRelicLevel(id, 0) on an equipped relic and via imports. The relic is inert and wastes a slot. The slot-count part of the second report is a separate issue: extraSlotsPurchased is not modelled, so the 4-slot cap is assumed. That part is unverified here and arguably [SERVER] state.
fixNotes: In reconcileRelics also drop ids whose character.relics[id] is 0 or absent, and call the reconcile from setRelicLevel. Add an ownership check to toggleRelic. Handle slot purchase separately.

title: Progression level gates (Awakening points, talent points, Transcendence, Dual Talents/Equip, Oblivion) are not enforced, and level changes do not re-reconcile
failureScenario: Repro (t3.mjs L1): a level-20 Warrior with awakening SHADOW 15, altarTier 8, Transcendence nodes and oblivion.unlocked + activeRealm 'oblivion' normalises unchanged, and the engine applies all of it. A level-50 character is allowed 15 Awakening points when the game caps it at 6, and 29 talent points at level 30 when the game allows 16. Lowering the level in the UI leaves a 3rd sigil equipped (and skill Oblivion levels) until reload.
proposedFix: Add level-derived caps in normalise/reconcile: awakening <= max(0, min(level,59)-44), talent points <= max(0, min(level,43)-14) per set, and zero Transcendence, Oblivion and second-set data below their unlock levels. Call reconcileCharacter from setCharacterLevel and setOblivionUnlocked.
corrected: Awakening points are not capped by character level (verified). The other gates (talent points, Transcendence, Dual Talents/Equip, Oblivion) are unchecked here and carried over from the finding. Level changes do not trigger reconcile (verified for setCharacterLevel).
fixNotes: Add level-derived caps in the normalise/reconcile step (awakening <= max(0, min(level,59)-44), talent points <= max(0, min(level,43)-14)). Call reconcile from setCharacterLevel. Consider warning rather than silently clamping, since imported profiles may have a stale level.

title: Ancient sigil ownership is decoupled from the Transcendence sigil node that grants it
failureScenario: A preset links a Transcendence preset without the Flameborn node but equips Flameborn, or the optimiser swaps transcendencePresetId to a preset lacking the node while keeping the Ancient. The model scores the +80% Attack transform that the game would have revoked.
proposedFix: Derive Ancient availability from the allocated sigil nodes of the preset's Transcendence preset (use the node to species map, L1068346). In reconcile, drop ancientSigilSpecies when the node is not allocated, and have the optimiser couple the two dimensions.

title: Sigil Altar tier accepts 4..8 although the game can only evolve to tier 3
failureScenario: Typing altar tier 8 multiplies every equipped sigil's flat Attack and HP by 3^7 = 2187 (sigils.md §4). That is a state no player can reach, and one slip in the data-entry control inflates all results. The same applies to opponents with altarTier up to 8.
proposedFix: Clamp to EVOLVE_TIER_CAP (or flag tiers above it as unverified). Reject Legendary sigils at tier 1 in reconcile.

title: Minor-glyph secondary accepts class-illegal stats and out-of-band quality
failureScenario: A Warrior glyph with Spell Crit Chance, or a Common glyph at quality 1.0 (an impossible roll worth 5x the maximum Common value), adds stats to the ridden mount that the game never rolls. Gear and pets are class-gated and glyphs are not.
proposedFix: Gate secondary.stat with available(statEnum, class) in normaliseGlyph (ctx.class) and clamp quality to GLYPH_QUALITY_BANDS[rarity], with Mythic fixed at 1. Reconcile on class change.
corrected: Minor-glyph secondary is not validated against the rarity quality band (Mythic must be 1, Common 0.1-0.2, and so on). It is also not validated against the class-eligible secondary pool. The band gap is [CODE]-backed. The class-pool gap is real in principle, but the exact per-class lists are partly [UNRESOLVED] in the docs. Impact is limited to manual-entry mistakes and stale glyphs after a class change.
fixNotes: Clamp quality to GLYPH_QUALITY_BANDS[rarity] (Mythic = 1) in normaliseSecondary. Add class gating only once stats.md has the full per-class lists. Until then, consider a UI warning rather than a hard drop.

title: Stone legality is minimal: stat pools, guaranteed stats, value ranges and Oblivion realm separation are unchecked, and sealed state is not stored
failureScenario: A typo or an edited export yields stones the game cannot roll (PvP stats on a Crimson stone, values over the stat max). An OBLIVION stone in the base pool, or an imported unactivated OBLIVION stone that gets socketed, adds 3250..50800 flat Attack and 10700..130500 flat HP when the game would count nothing or put it in the other realm.
proposedFix: In normaliseStone, check each stat against the type's pool and the guaranteed list, clamp values to [min, max] (decimals applied) and cap the count. Reject OBLIVION in the base pool and non-OBLIVION in the Oblivion pool. Persist activated, or drop unactivated stones on import.
corrected: The gaps in the finding exist as described. They are limited to imported or hand-edited data, and the 'unactivated Oblivion stone' scenario needs a game-profile import that carries such a stone. The 'sealed state not stored' part could be stated more narrowly: the engine only skips stones with an explicit activated === false, and the normalised model never sets that field. The second report is also right: the stat count is capped at statCount, and the stats kept depend on input order, so a guaranteed stat listed last can be lost.
fixNotes: Validate each stat against the type's pool and guaranteed list in normaliseStone. Clamp values to the [min, max] range for that stat. Keep the stat order deterministic, with guaranteed stats first. Reject OBLIVION in the base list and non-OBLIVION in the Oblivion list. Either persist activated or drop sealed stones on import.

title: Gear caps are not game-derived: item-level cap ignores Ascension, secondary values have no ceiling, conduit type and Oblivion minimum rarity are unchecked
failureScenario: Drop Check can compare a level-240 or 99% Crit drop for a player with Ascension 1 (cap 100), or a DARK-conduit Eternal base item. The verdict is for an item that cannot exist, and quality is computed against the wrong ceiling.
proposedFix: Take the item-level cap from skills.ascension (and the realm table), clamp secondary values to secondaryStatMaxValue(def, statLevel), enforce the conduit type per rarity and realm, and floor Oblivion-realm rarity at Mythic.
corrected: Confirmed for the item-level cap (ignores Ascension) and the missing secondary-value ceiling. The conduit-type-per-rarity and Oblivion Mythic-floor parts I did not verify. The behaviour is lenient by design and low impact: Ascension caps drops, not owned items, and the game's watermark logic is server-side. Severity stays minor.
fixNotes: Cap itemLevel by the character's skills.ascension using data/gear.json maxItemLevelByAscension. Warn or clamp (rather than silently drop) secondary values above secondaryStatMaxValue(def, statLevel). Restrict conduit type by rarity and realm. Keep the leniency for null-rarity and migrated data.

title: Importing any unrecognised JSON replaces the whole roster with an empty one, with no error
failureScenario: Scratch run (audit/model-accuracy/imp.mjs): `importJson('{}')`, `'[]'`, `'{"foo":1}'` and a near-profile `{"player":{"class":"WARRIOR","level":50}}` (no `equipment`, so isGameProfile is false) all return kind 'roster' with 0 characters. A user who picks the wrong JSON file, or a game-profile capture that fails the strict isGameProfile markers (level sent as a string, no `equipment` object, wrapped in an envelope), loses every saved character. The empty roster is persisted immediately and nothing asks for confirmation.
proposedFix: In importJson/importFromJson, if the parsed value is not a game profile and normaliseRoster yields zero characters, throw so the Sidebar's catch shows 'Import failed'. Only call setRoster for a roster that has at least one character. Consider confirming before replacing a non-empty roster. Keep normaliseRoster's empty-roster fallback for loadRoster only.
corrected: Confirmed as stated. The harm is on the Sidebar import path only, where a non-empty roster is replaced. On the WelcomeScreen the roster is already empty, so nothing is lost, though the user still gets no error for a bad file. | Confirmed as stated. Importing JSON that is neither a game profile nor a roster with at least one character silently replaces and persists an empty roster. Nothing throws, so the UI's 'Import failed' message never shows.
fixNotes: In importJson's non-profile branch, throw when normaliseRoster yields zero characters. Keep the empty-roster fallback in loadRoster. Optionally confirm before replacing a non-empty roster. Add a rosterStore test that `{}` throws and leaves the roster unchanged. | In importJson, throw when the parsed value is not a game profile and normaliseRoster returns zero characters. Keep the empty-roster fallback for loadRoster only. Optionally ask for confirmation before replacing a non-empty roster. Update the storage.test.js:128 expectation for junk input, and add a rosterStore test that a junk import leaves the existing roster untouched.

title: normaliseLevel maps an empty or null level to 1 (but undefined or NaN to 100), and level 1 then silently wipes every preset's sigil equips on the next load or edit
failureScenario: Scratch run (lvl.mjs): on the real L72 character, normaliseLevel('') = 1. Re-normalising with level 1 changes presets from [3,3] sigils to [0,0], even though sigils.owned is kept. Level 20 gives the same result. The user clears the field, tabs away and reloads (or edits any preset, which calls reconcile). Their sigil loadouts are gone and typing 100 back does not restore them. The same call path treats undefined as 100, so the default is inconsistent.
proposedFix: Treat '', null, false and arrays as invalid in normaliseLevel (`if (raw === '' || raw == null || typeof raw === 'boolean') return MAX_PLAYER_LEVEL`, or keep the previous level in setCharacterLevel). Consider not destroying equips when the level falls below an unlock: keep them and let the build layer ignore them.
corrected: An empty or null level input is normalised to 1 rather than to the undefined/NaN default of 100. This is reachable through the Level input in the UI. Level 1 then clears the sigil equips on every preset. That wipe is irreversible, and re-entering the old level does not bring the equips back. Wiping on a genuinely low level is the intended gate, so the real bug is limited to the empty-input path and to the equips not being kept.
fixNotes: In normaliseLevel, treat '', null and booleans as invalid and return MAX_PLAYER_LEVEL, or have onLevel ignore empty input. Optionally keep the equips when the level drops and let the build layer ignore the locked slots.

title: Conduit type is not checked against item rarity and realm
failureScenario: Scratch run (cond.mjs): `normaliseItem` keeps ETERNAL+DARK in the base realm, ETERNAL+FLAME and DIVINE+FLAME in the Oblivion realm, and OBLIVION+FLAME in the base realm. Totals then add to totalDarkConduit or totalFlameConduit that the game cannot produce, and the chrono-flux model (pve/fight.js:711-736) charges differently. The state is reachable by v2 import or hand edit, and by the Drop Check item entry.
proposedFix: Add `conduitTypesFor(rarity, realm)`: base ETERNAL -> [FLAME, EARTHEN], base OBLIVION -> [DARK], oblivion realm >= DIVINE -> [DARK]. Drop or coerce other types in normaliseItem.
corrected: As stated. Additional detail: in the Oblivion realm an exactly-ETERNAL item (below the DARK minimum rarity) can still carry Flame/Earthen, so only rarities >= DARK_CONDUIT_MIN_RARITY there are DARK-only. The fix must follow the client's branch order.
fixNotes: Add conduitTypesFor(rarity, realm) mirroring the client. In the oblivion realm with rarity >= DARK_CONDUIT_MIN_RARITY the only type is DARK. Otherwise ETERNAL gives [FLAME, EARTHEN], OBLIVION gives [DARK], and anything else gives none. In normaliseItem, drop the conduit when its type is not in that list, or coerce it. Keep the rarity == null leniency. Add a test.

title: Per-character run-history budget (1.5 MB) is not a roster-wide budget, but the whole roster is one localStorage value whose quota failures are swallowed
failureScenario: Three or four characters that each approach the history budget (50 detailed runs plus up to 2000 rows) exceed about 5 MB. setItem throws and is swallowed, so every later edit appears to work but is lost on reload (stale blob), with no warning. The roster that was last saved successfully is what returns. The budget also stringifies the whole history once per detail dropped, which is O(n squared) on load.
proposedFix: Budget across the roster (total serialised size) in the roster-level save, surface a visible warning when setItem fails, and drop detail in one pass using per-run size estimates.
corrected: The per-character run budget is not a roster-wide budget, and saveRoster silently ignores quota errors. Loss of unsaved edits needs the total roster to exceed about 5M characters, which realistically takes several characters with very large histories (or heavy other data). The quadratic stringify is bounded by the roughly 50 detailed runs that survive compactRuns.
fixNotes: Have saveRoster return a success flag or surface a visible warning on setItem failure. Optionally apply a roster-level size check and trim run detail across characters. Drop detail using per-run size estimates instead of re-stringifying the whole list on each pass.
